text:
sarah: quick check — we've got four candidate models to onboard next quarter (phoenix-8k, atlas-13b, mixr-7b-quant, helper-code-4b). thinking about sequencing by signal vs noise rather than pure RICE. any strong opinions?
kevin: i'd bias toward customer signals first. phoenix-8k is requested by two large customers and improves convo latency, so high impact + lower infra work.
tina: agree on phoenix. atlas-13b looks promising for embeddings use-cases (search + rerank) but needs quant pipeline and perf tuning — higher effort.
sarah: here's a quick RICE-ish sketch i made, feel free to poke holes:
```
Model            Reach  Impact  Confidence  Effort(days)  RICE_score
phoenix-8k       30     7        0.8        10            168
atlas-13b        20     6        0.6        18            40.0
mixr-7b-quant    15     5        0.7         8             65.6
helper-code-4b   10     4        0.9         5             72.0
```
kevin: nice. hotspot: atlas has medium reach but large downstream infra risk (quant + perf regressions). that kills confidence for me.
ben: note — atlas will also unlock internal embeddings migration which reduces costs long-term (indirect impact). maybe we should add a deferred benefit multiplier?
sarah: good point. we should record deferred/capacity benefits in notes (not inflate immediate RICE).
mia: small flag — helper-code-4b is low-effort and customers love faster code completions; good quick win for platform demos and case studies. :rocket:
tina: sequencing suggestion: 1) phoenix-8k (customer requested, low effort) 2) helper-code-4b (quick win) 3) mixr-7b-quant (cost win + solid perf) 4) atlas-13b (big infra work, schedule into Q2 reserve).
kevin: +1 to that order. we should also gate atlas with a rollout plan: canary on dedicated, automated fallback to atlas-quant -> atlas-fp16, and a regression eval set.
sarah: action items: kevin to draft atlas rollout playbook (due Tue), ben to quantify deferred cost savings for atlas (Econ doc), tina to scope quant infra changes (ETA 5 business days). i'll file tickets and add to roadmap.
release-bot: note — planned onboarding may affect Dedicated capacity reservations. Please coordinate with eng-ops.
ben: i'll ping eng-ops after econ doc.
sarah: thanks team. if no objections i'll lock sequence into the roadmap by EOD and update the onboarding checklist with the gating criteria (metrics: latency p95, token cost delta, accuracy on eval set).
kevin: no objections from me.
tina: ok from me.
mia: thumbs up.
sarah: closing thread — will post updated roadmap link when done. :white_check_mark:
